raw_record.question_text:
The region shown in the figure below has widespread frozen soil. Frozen soil mainly includes permafrost and seasonal frozen soil. The number of seasonal frozen-soil days refers to the number of days when water in the soil layer is frozen. Read the figure and answer the following question.

<image1>

Assuming that the weather system in the figure moves eastward at a speed of 120 kilometers/day, how will the wind force at place A change in the next 30h?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the labeled isobars 1030.0 hPa, 1027.5 hPa, and 1025.0 hPa and locate 甲 near the 1027.5 hPa line; note that the isobars west/northwest of 甲 are denser. From the text, take the eastward movement speed of the whole weather system and the time interval of 30 h. Calculate that the system will move east about 150 km. Mentally shift the whole isobar pattern east by this distance while keeping 甲 fixed. After the shift, the originally denser isobar zone west of 甲 will be closer to or over 甲, so the pressure gradient at 甲 will become larger. Conclude that the wind force at 甲 will strengthen.
